### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is IGI Global's PUBLISHER-WIDE policy (no journal-level AI policy page found for IJMHCI itself). Facts: (1) Authors may use generative AI/AI-assisted tools for data-analysis support and for improving readability (translation, grammar, language polish), but must maintain oversight/control and disclose the tool and how it was used in an AI-disclosure statement included in every manuscript -> disclosure-gated, not free-use, not outright banned. (2) AI-generated images or videos are explicitly prohibited. (3) Editors/reviewers are barred from uploading unpublished manuscripts to generative AI tools (confidentiality breach). |
| **Source URL** | https://www.igi-global.com/publish/contributor-resources/open-access-journal-editorial-policy/ (also referenced: https://www.igi-global.com/newsroom/archive/don-let-write-your-credibility/6649/) |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Conditional / discouraged at submission. IGI Global's open-access journal editorial policy states manuscripts posted openly on repositories such as ResearchGate, SSRN, or arXiv 'should not be considered until they have been removed from those respective sites' -- i.e., concurrent preprints block consideration for review. A separate, lower-confidence search result (not independently verified against a live SHERPA/RoMEO record page) suggested IGI Global permits preprint deposit post-acceptance if the deposited copy states it has not undergone peer review and cites the published version. These two facts describe different stages (pre-submission vs. post-acceptance) and were not reconciled against one authoritative page.
> Source: https://www.igi-global.com/publish/contributor-resources/open-access-journal-editorial-policy/

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Recent 2025-2026 published articles skew toward quantitative/computational methods applied to mobile-device user behavior and media/tourism/driving contexts rather than classic qualitative UX fieldwork.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Machine learning / classification analysis of user behavior (e.g., 'Behavioral Classification of Mobile Device Users in Digital Communication Contexts,' 2026), Computer vision frameworks for interactive visual communication in mobile environments (2026), Mixed-methods field trials of human-AI collaborative systems (e.g., 'Human-AI Collaborative Recommenders for On-Site Cultural Tourism,' 2025), Customer/user satisfaction survey analysis (e.g., mobile games satisfaction study, 2025), Driver cognitive-preference / in-vehicle HCI studies (2025), Case studies on handheld/mobile/wearable technology design and evaluation (long-standing journal scope per aims & scope)

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **experiential.review_time_months**: No SciRev entry found for this journal (searches for the exact title on scirev.org returned no dedicated journal page); LetPub's dedicated page for this journal has an empty user-submitted review-speed field (0 data points).
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No SciRev entry and no forum/community post (小木虫, 知乎, Reddit r/AskAcademia) discussing desk-reject rate for this specific journal was found; only publisher-wide generic IGI Global timelines exist, which are policy claims not experiential reports.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No first-hand reviewer-experience narrative found in 小木虫 muchong.com, 知乎, fabiaoji, or Reddit specifically naming this journal (searches returned only generic journal-metadata pages, or results for the differently-titled Taylor & Francis 'International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction', which is a different journal and was excluded to avoid conflation).
- **ai_policy (journal-specific layer)**: No IJMHCI-specific AI-use policy page was found; the AI policy reported is IGI Global's publisher-wide policy applied to all its journals, not a policy tailored to IJMHCI.
- **preprint.allowed (precise mechanism)**: Found two partially conflicting fragments (pre-submission preprint-site restriction vs. general SHERPA/RoMEO-style post-acceptance archiving rights) that were not reconciled against one authoritative IGI Global preprint-specific policy page; treat with reduced confidence.
